abstract: To realize spoken dialogue systems that can interact naturally with users, it is important for the system to respond to user utterances at appropriate timings. To achieve such natural turn-taking, the system needs not only to predict appropriate response timings but also to mask delays caused by language generation and speech synthesis so that they are not perceived by the user. We propose a real-time short-response selection task that can be integrated with existing turn-taking models to mask generation delay. To address this task, the proposed model learns the mapping between dialogue context and short responses using contrastive learning. When a turn-taking event is detected, the system selects a response from a set of pre-generated candidates. The selected response is played while the main response is being generated. Experimental results show that the proposed method learns to select short responses based on dialogue context, outperforming random and LLM-based baselines. Moreover, integrating response selection maintained turn-taking prediction performance and added minimal processing overhead.

oneSentenceThesis: 论文把轮流发言预测与短回复选择放在同一流式语音编码器上，用对比学习把对话上下文和预生成的短语音对齐，在检测到发言时机时先播放短回复以掩盖大模型与语音合成的延迟，实验显示选择优于随机与基于文本的大模型基线且几乎不增加耗时。
originalTitle: Real-Time Short-Response Selection for Spoken Dialogue Systems
readerTitle: 不等大模型说完就先开口：实时短回复选择如何掩盖对话系统延迟
